Hold this box back from today’s destruction batch, and release the other 59 on time.

The extension request is not permission, the booking does not by itself change the date, and a discretionary extension is outside both OPS-14 and this morning’s instruction. That is all true. It is also true that Claire Morgan’s ID and authority are already checked, collection is booked for Wednesday 10:00, and the notes say these letters and photos were never copied. Destruction at 14:30 cannot be undone. The only reason the request is still pending is that approval sittings are Tuesday and Thursday; the next one is tomorrow, after the contents would already be gone.

Do not fail the whole manifest to save one box. Before 13:30, change this box’s date so it is pulled from the cage into reserve (the about EUR 22 rework), release the rest of the batch by 13:30, and write up the breach in full for the duty manager and the monthly audit: what was done, why, and that it was not authorised in advance. Ask them to ratify or reverse it at tomorrow’s 09:00 sitting, while the box still exists.

A later permission cannot bless an earlier date change, and the audit should record this as an exception, not as compliance. A EUR 22 unauthorised hold is the smaller wrong. Destroying the only copies of a late parent’s letters and photographs, two days before an already authorised collection, is not.
